content.title: Celtics-Knicks recap: Scheierman shines, but C's fall in thriller at MSG
content.text: What to KnowChris Forsberg and Kayla Burton shared more postgame reaction on the Celtics Talk Podcast.Knicks won season series vs. Celtics, 3-1.Josh Hart scored a game-high 26 points (10-15 FG, 5-7 3-PT) for Knicks.Jayson Tatum notched 24 points, 13 rebounds, and eight assists in return to MSG.Payton Pritchard (23 points) and Baylor Scheierman (20 points, 6-7 3-PT) stepped up for Boston. The Boston Celtics came up short against the New York Knicks in what may have been a second-round playoff preview at Madison Square Garden, 112-106. With Jaylen Brown out, Baylor Scheierman stepped up off the C's bench with 20 points on 6-of-7 shooting from deep in a losing effort. Payton Pritchard added 23 points for the second unit. Jayson Tatum nearly notched a triple-double with 24 points, 13 rebounds, and eight assists. Josh Hart propelled the Knicks to victory with a game-high 26 points (5-7 3-PT). Check out our live blog below for a full recap of Thursday night's game: The Boston Celtics fell to the New York Knicks in Thursday night's showdown at Madison Square Garden, 112-106. It was a back-and-forth affair between the Eastern Conference rivals, featuring 16 lead changes and 13 ties. The Knicks actually led by as many as 13 points in the third quarter, but the C's responded quickly to retake the lead in the frame. From there, it was a nail-biter. Baylor Scheierman scored 11 of his 20 points in the fourth quarter to keep the Celtics alive, but Josh Hart was even hotter with 15 of his 26 points coming in the fourth. Hart added a dagger 3-pointer with 15 seconds remaining. Although it came in a losing effort, Scheierman delivered an exceptional performance. He stepped up with Jaylen Brown (left Achilles tendinitis) out, shooting 6-of-7 from 3-point range. “It was a big moment, a big hurdle for me," the Celtics star said of his first game at Madison Square Garden since his injury. "I was nervous and anxious to come back here. "... I wanted to walk off the court on my own two feet." Payton Pritchard is prepared for a potential playoff rematch with the Knicks. "If we see them again, we'll be ready," the Celtics sharpshooter said after Thursday's loss: Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla praised Baylor Scheierman after his big night, which including 20 points on six 3-pointers. “Obviously, shot-making is the easiest thing to see and helps us on the scoreboard, but he just does a lot for us," Mazzulla said. "Whether it's his crashing or his defense, but his instincts on both ends. … He just continues to get better and better, and that's what we need, hitting that stretch there.“ Knicks star Jalen Brunson spoke after the game about Jayson Tatum's return from his Achilles tear: Score: 109-104 Knicks, 42.4 seconds left in the fourth quarter Josh Hart drilled a 3-pointer to extend the Knicks' lead to five with 42 seconds to go. He has 23 points on 9-of-14 shooting (4-6 3-PT). Score: 105-104 Knicks, 1:26 left in fourth quarter The Knicks have a one-point lead with just over a minute left, but Baylor Scheierman has done his part to keep the Celtics within striking distance. Scheierman has 20 points on 6-of-7 shooting from 3-point range. He has 11 points here in the fourth. Score: 92-90 Celtics, 6:48 left in the fourth quarter The Celtics are clinging to a two-point lead midway through the fourth after trailing by 13 in the third. Jayson Tatum has struggled from 3 (2-10), but it otherwise has been a great game for the C's star. He has 24 points, `12 rebounds, and seven assists in 33 minutes. Payton Pritchard has been the star for Boston, delivering 23 points (10-18 FG) and four assists off the bench. Baylor Scheierman has also made an impact off the bench with 12 points on 4-of-5 shooting from deep. Score: 83-81 Celtics The Celtics trailed by 13 in the third quarter, but they'll take a two-point lead into the fourth after a furious comeback. Payton Pritchard has led the way for Boston with a game-high 23 points on 10-of-17 shooting (3-6 3-PT). Jayson Tatum is flirting with a triple-double, tallying 18 points with 12 rebounds and seven assists. Nikola Vucevic (eight points) and Baylor Scheierman (nine points) made big shots from beyond the arc in the third. Score: 76-72 Knicks, 3:21 left in third quarter The Celtics have cut their 13-point deficit to four with a 13-4 run. Nikola Vucevic, Baylor Scheierman and Payton Pritchard made timely 3-pointers Pritchard and Jayson Tatum lead Boston with 18 points apiece. Patriots owner Robert Kraft is taking in the action courtside at Madison Square Garden: Score: 72-59 Knicks, 6:57 left in third quarter The Knicks are getting pretty much anything they want both inside and beyond the arc. Karl-Anthony Towns (nine points, 11 rebounds) bullied Boston in the paint on back-to-back possessions to widen New York's lead to 13. Score: 66-57 Knicks, 9:32 left in the third quarter The Knicks are on a 12-4 run to begin the second half. Josh Hart started the third with a pair of 3s, while OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges both added 3s of their own. Threes have been an issue for the Celtics so far in this one. They're just 5-of-21 from deep, while the Knicks are 11-of-25. Score: 54-53 Knicks The Celtics trail by one after a fun first half at Madison Square Garden. Jayson Tatum nearly notched a double-double in the first 24 minutes, logging 10 points and nine rebounds to go with four assists. Payton Pritchard paced the C's with 15 points (7-12 FG) off the bench, while Neemias Queta added eight points and seven boards. Jalen Brunson (16 points) and OG Anunoby (10 points) have led the Knicks in the scoring column. Neither team has shot great from 3-point range, with the Celtics going 5-of-21 from deep and the Knicks shooting 7-of-21 from beyond the arc. Score: 40-38 Celtics, 5:36 left in second quarter After allowing the Knicks to go on a 12-2 run, the Celtics responded with a 7-0 run before New York's timeout to pull back ahead. It has been an entertaining start at Madison Square Garden. Payton Pritchard has stepped up off the C's bench with 15 points (7-10 FG), while Jayson Tatum has delivered 10 points and nine rebounds. Celtics big man Nikola Vucevic has struggled in the first half. In eight minutes, he's a -6 with zero points and a turnover. Jalen Brunson and OG Anunoby lead the Knicks with 10 and seven points, respectively. Score: 35-31 Knicks, 8:48 left in second quarter The Knicks are on a 12-2 run going back to the end of the first. The Celtics have yet to make a field goal in the frame. Score: 29-26 Celtics The first quarter between these Eastern Conference contenders did not disappoint. Payton Pritchard starred off the Celtics' bench with a game-high 11 points on 5-of-7 shooting. He drilled his first 3-pointer of the night just before the end of the frame, but Jalen Brunson (10 points) responded with one of his own just before the buzzer. Jayson Tatum has six points, six rebounds, and two assists through nine minutes in his first game at Madison Square Garden since his injury. Neemias Queta chipped in four points and four rebounds. Mikal Bridges scored the Knicks' first seven points of the game but hasn't made a bucket since. Score: 21-14 Celtics, 2:44 left in first quarter Payton Pritchard has come off the C's bench and delivered a quick six points (3-4 FG) to extend Boston's lead to seven. Score: 13-11 Celtics, 5:54 left in first quarter Jayson Tatum is back at Madison Square Garden for the first time since suffering his Achilles tear there last May. It's a mental hurdle for the C's star, but he hasn't shown any signs of struggle so far. Tatum has six points and six rebounds through the first six minutes of action. He also notched a steal. Neemias Queta has four points and two rebounds for Boston. Jordan Walsh added a 3-pointer. Celtics: Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Sam Hauser, Jayson Tatum, Neemias Queta Knicks: Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby, Josh Hart, Karl-Anthony Towns Jayson Tatum NAILED his trick shot before his first game back at Madison Square Garden since his Achilles injury. Watch below: Jordan Walsh spoke about Celtics teammate Jayson Tatum's return from injury in an exclusive interview with NBC Sports Boston's Abby Chin. "He's special. He's a machine. He came back really quickly. He wanted to play, he wanted to win, he wanted to try and get us to the next level." Watch the full clip below: Abby Chin caught up with Jordan Walsh ahead of the Celtics' matchup with the Knicks at Madison Square garden, and Walsh talked about Jayson Tatum's return. Knicks coach Mike Brown spoke pregame about Jayson Tatum's return from injury, praising the Celitcs star for his "drive" and "determination." "He's worked his tail off to be back to where he is. He was a great player before, he's going to be a great player after," Brown said. "It's amazing that he's back playing at this level going into the playoffs in this short amount of time. That's just his drive, determination, and competitive spirit all showing its face at the right time. "I hope they lose every game.. but I'm happy for him individually." Celtics Jaylen Brown (left Achilles tendinitis) - OUT Derrick White (right knee contusion) - AVAILABLE Sam Hauser (low back spasm) - AVAILABLE Neemias Queta (right toe sprain) - AVAILABLE Knicks Tyler Kolek (oblique) - OUT Jayson Tatum is back at Madison Square Garden for the first time since suffering his Achilles injury there last May. He admitted that he's "not thrilled" about the mental hurdle of returning to MSG, but he's ready to "face the challenge head-on." Chris Forsberg talks with Hall of Famer and NBC Studio Analyst Tracy McGrady about his new one-on-one league in Atlanta, his relationship with Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum’s first month back, and where the Celtics stand in the East. The 2018-19 NBA season was a tough one for the Boston Celtics. They went into that campaign with championship expectations, but for many reasons, that goal wasn't achieved. The C's playoff run ended in a five-game loss to the Milwaukee Bucks in the Eastern Conference semifinals. A few months later, Kyrie Irving and Al Horford left in free agency. It was also a difficult season for Jaylen Brown. He took a huge step in his development during the 2017-18 season, especially in the playoffs when he played a prominent role with Irving and Gordon Hayward sidelined due to injuries. The Celtics advanced all the way to Game 7 of the 2018 Eastern Conference Finals. Brown saw his playing time and many of his stats decrease in 2018-19. He also went from making 70 starts in 2017-18 to just 25 in 2018-19. Read Full Article
